You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 51b75b5b563a2637f9d8dc5bd02a31b2ff9e5ea0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Joerg Roedel <jroedel@suse.de>
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2019 20:46:50 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] x86/mm: Check for pfn instead of page in vmalloc_sync_one()

Do not require a struct page for the mapped memory location because it
might not exist. This can happen when an ioremapped region is mapped with
2MB pages.

Fixes: 5d72b4fba40ef ('x86, mm: support huge I/O mapping capability I/F')
Signed-off-by: Joerg Roedel <jroedel@suse.de>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Reviewed-by: Dave Hansen <dave.hansen@linux.intel.com>
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20190719184652.11391-2-joro@8bytes.org
---
 arch/x86/mm/fault.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/arch/x86/mm/fault.c b/arch/x86/mm/fault.c
index 6c46095cd0d9..e64173db4970 100644
--- a/arch/x86/mm/fault.c
+++ b/arch/x86/mm/fault.c
@@ -183,7 +183,7 @@ static inline pmd_t *vmalloc_sync_one(pgd_t *pgd, unsigned long address)
 	if (!pmd_present(*pmd))
 		set_pmd(pmd, *pmd_k);
 	else
-		BUG_ON(pmd_page(*pmd) != pmd_page(*pmd_k));
+		BUG_ON(pmd_pfn(*pmd) != pmd_pfn(*pmd_k));
 
 	return pmd_k;
 }
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by the assumption that a struct page would always be available for the mapped memory location in the `vmalloc_sync_one()` function. This assumption fails when dealing with ioremapped regions that are mapped using 2MB pages, where a struct page may not exist. The patch corrects this by checking the page frame number (pfn) instead of the struct page, ensuring that the function can handle cases where the struct page is not present.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by the assumption that a struct page would always be available for the mapped memory location in the `vmalloc_sync_one()` function. This assumption fails when dealing with ioremapped regions that are mapped using 2MB pages, where a struct page may not exist. The patch corrects this by checking the page frame number (pfn) instead of the struct page, ensuring that the function can handle cases where the struct page is not present.
